findings.finding: AC-7 has no `rc 5` / gone-test fallback for the resume path. In-run retry has AC-2's rc-5 fallback, but a resumed run's `--lf --lfnf=none` can select nothing when a red test was deleted or renamed between invocations (arguably the most common fix pattern — the operator deletes a bad test, or a parametrize id changes). Then pytest exits 5, and the spec is silent on what happens: the unit could be miscounted green, or the run could fail confusingly.
findings.suggestion: Mirror AC-2 on the resume path: rc 5 (or lastfailed entries that no longer resolve) → re-run the unit whole, serially. State it explicitly in AC-7 so it isn't discovered at implementation time.  2. Category: security — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The resume state path is derived from the operator-supplied `--run-id` (`<main-root>/.shipwright/runs/f0-resume/<key(run_id)>/`). If `key()` is not a slug/hash, a run-id like `../../repo` or an absolute-path-shaped string writes/copies state outside the intended directory (and `load_state` would read attacker-adjacent paths — lower risk since it's the same operator, but the write/restore-coverage path makes it worth one line of defense).
findings.suggestion: Make `key(run_id)` an actual hash (sha256 hex) or strictly validated slug `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` with no path separators. One function, no cost.  3. Category: risk — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Coverage path identity across invocations. `purge_files` and `--cov-append` match on stored file paths, and the design copies per-unit coverage data files from the resume state into a new run's temp dirs. If any paths in the `.coverage` data are absolute (e.g., unit tmp dirs, or absolute source paths depending on how `build_command` sets up coverage), purge of changed files and appends silently miss, producing either stale coverage (the exact false-attribute problem AC-8 exists to prevent) or double-counting. The probes verified `purge_files` works on same-session data; they don't establish cross-session path stability.
findings.suggestion: Add a probe/assertion that the copied baseline `.coverage` files record paths that match the resumed run's working tree (relative to the same repo root), and fail closed to a full run if they don't. Fold this into AC-10's integration test (check coverage of the fixed file comes only from run 2).  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: AC-4's merge keys testcases by `classname+name`. Parametrized tests produce multiple testcases sharing name-with-params usually, fine — but a unit can legitimately contain duplicate classname+name pairs (same parametrize id under different rootdir prefixes, or `__init__`-collected names), where blind replacement corrupts counts (the "test totals stay the whole unit's" guarantee). Also: if the first attempt's JUnit has a `<testsuite>`-level error (collection error producing no per-test testcases), the cross-check count (0 failed testcases vs N lastfailed) will fail and you fall back — good — but merge must not be attempted on partially-written reports either.
findings.suggestion: In `merge_junit`, verify the replacement set exactly matches re-run testcase keys one-to-one; on any mismatch (duplicates, unmatched, count drift), fall back to retaining the retry report alone plus a marker, or the whole-unit path. Make mismatch → fallback explicit rather than best-effort replacement.  5. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: First attempt switches from `-p no:cacheprovider` to `-o cache_dir=<unit tmp>/c`. Two things to confirm: (a) unit tmp dirs are cleaned between invocations, so `--lf` can never pick up stale lastfailed from a previous F0 invocation of the same unit within the same process/run ordering; (b) the cache plugin being enabled doesn't change behavior for tests that currently assert on the exact pytest argv (existing fake-`_exec` tests may pin argv strings).
findings.suggestion: Explicit AC/test: cache dir is fresh per attempt, and existing argv-pinning tests are updated in step 4 (the refactor step) rather than silently changed.  6. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Resume state pruning "newest 5 on save" plus "deleted on green" is fine, but two F0 invocations with the same run-id running concurrently (or a resumed run crashing mid-save) can leave a torn state dir (partial JSON, half-copied coverage). AC-6 says invalid state → full run, which covers reads — but only if `load_state` validates atomically (checksum on the manifest, or write-to-temp-then-rename).
findings.suggestion: Save atomically: write the state dir under a temp name and rename; treat any missing manifest field as invalid.  7. Category: approach — Severity: low

findings.finding: AC-7's "changed test files of that unit as a second appended invocation" means a resumed red unit can run two pytest invocations (lastfailed, then changed files). A test file that changed may also contain the red test — it runs twice in the second invocation. Harmless for the union coverage and merged report (same key replaced twice), but worth a stated rule so the report merge and `Retention` dedupe deterministically (last wins).
findings.suggestion: Document "retry-later invocation wins on key collision" in `merge_junit` and add a unit test for the double-run-of-one-testcase case.  8. Category: over-production — Severity: low

findings.finding: Mostly proportionate. The only mild flag: three new modules plus injected-callable indirection in `suite_retry` is borderline, but it's justified by AC-11's 529-line bloat cap and keeping monkeypatch seams — not needless. No new dependencies. Fine as is.  Overall assessment: The approach is sound and unusually well-probed (lastfailed under xdist, purge_files, rc-5 semantics all verified), with the right fallback-first philosophy. The gaps are all in the resume path — no rc-5/gone-test fallback (finding 1), path-traversal in the state key (finding 2), and cross-session coverage path identity (finding 3) — all cheap to fix and worth fixing before implementation.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

The five-file threshold does not make reuse of PASS units safe. A one-line shared-library fix can break a previously green unit. Purging changed-file coverage prevents stale coverage attribution, but does not detect behavioral regressions. The rejected alternative’s risk therefore remains in the proposed approach.
findings.suggestion: Describe a resumed green result as incremental evidence and ensure downstream consumers cannot treat it as a fresh full-suite pass. If F0 must certify current whole-suite correctness, invalidate affected units or run the full suite after source changes.

findings.finding: Removed or renamed tests are counted as eligible changes, but report merging only replaces matching testcase keys. Old testcases can survive indefinitely; a removed failing test can remain red after a whole-unit fallback unless that report replaces the baseline entirely.
findings.suggestion: Force a whole-unit run for units containing removed or renamed test files, replacing their baseline reports. Define how changed files that remove individual tests invalidate old testcase entries.

findings.finding: Resume validation is underspecified for reused PASS units and failed-only selection. Missing PASS coverage or reports can produce incomplete aggregate evidence. A readable but empty or stale red-unit cache can select no tests, and the resume path does not explicitly apply the in-run cross-check and rc-5 fallback.
findings.suggestion: Validate every reused unit’s required artifacts, cross-check red-unit caches against retained reports, and apply whole-unit fallback on invalid selection or rc 5 during resume. Keep collection errors, subprocess failures, and failures from either appended invocation red regardless of later report replacements.

findings.finding: Copying cache, coverage, XML, and metadata into one run-id directory can leave a mixed or partial baseline after interruption or concurrent invocations. Pruning another invocation’s active state is also possible.
findings.suggestion: Save complete snapshots to a staging directory and publish atomically. Serialize access per run-id, record a schema version and unit/configuration identity, and exclude active snapshots from pruning.

findings.finding: The stated verification command targets `shared/scripts/tools/tests`, while the real-pytest test is listed under `integration-tests`. Nothing in the plan establishes that CI collects this required probe or provisions its subprocess dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit integration-test command and CI collection/provisioning step. Extend the probe to cover changed test files, removed tests, corrupted state, rc-5 fallback, and changed-source coverage purging.  The failed-only retry approach is sound, and the extraction preserves useful compatibility seams. Resume needs stronger evidence semantics, artifact validation, and report invalidation rules before implementation can safely proceed.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: _exec passes a cache dir to every attempt, so the pytest cacheprovider is on everywhere; the printed reproduce command still says -p no:cacheprovider.
findings.suggestion: Disclosed in F0.md (accepted: the narrow retry needs the first attempt's cache).

findings.finding: merge_junit recomputes totals on suites[0] only.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: returns False (whole-unit fallback) for a multi-suite report.

findings.finding: 'failed-only' literal duplicated.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: RETRY_FAILED_ONLY imported.

findings.finding: Fallback list omits the short re-run trigger.
findings.suggestion: FIXED in docs and F0.md.

findings.finding: The whole-unit fallback exec (after rc 5 / unmergeable report / INFRA-classified narrow retry) runs outside the `ops.heartbeat_fn(...)` context — only the first (narrow) exec is wrapped. The fallback is precisely the ~22-minute authoritative run the heartbeats exist to make visible, so during it the run emits no `serial-retry` heartbeats.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the fallback second `_exec` in its own heartbeat context (same params), or move both execs inside one heartbeat block.

findings.finding: When a narrow retry falls back to the whole-unit path, the start and complete events are emitted with `retry_kind=state` which still says `"failed-only"`, while `res.retry_kind` ends as `"serial"`. Telemetry/heartbeat consumers see a retry kind the result does not carry — AC-2 says the fallback must be "exactly as today".
findings.suggestion: Recompute `state` (or emit `res.retry_kind`) before the complete event once the fallback has fired.

findings.finding: AC-1 literally states a green failed-only retry is `race=True, retry_kind="serial"` "exactly as today", but the implementation (and the tests) use `retry_kind="failed-only"`. The plan-review section clearly resolved this to a distinct kind, so the code follows the later decision — but the AC text and the code disagree; one of them should be amended so the acceptance check isn't ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Update AC-1's wording (or note the plan-review amendment inline) to `retry_kind="failed-only"`.

findings.finding: When the base report has multiple `<testsuite>` elements, re-run testcases are appended only to `suites[0]`, yet `tests/failures/errors/skipped` totals are recomputed across all suites and written onto `suites[0]` only — other suites keep stale totals and the first suite's totals are inflated. pytest's junit_xml normally emits one suite, so this is latent, but `stage_f0_evidence`'s "complete and green" rule reads those attributes.
findings.suggestion: Either reject multi-suite bases (return False → whole-unit fallback) or recompute per-suite totals per suite.

findings.finding: Because `_exec` defaults the cache dir for every call, the whole-unit serial retry and the INFRA identical-shape retry now run with `-o cache_dir=<tmp>/c` instead of today's `-p no:cacheprovider`. That's benign (fresh per-attempt tmp) and keeps AC-6's "never the repo `.pytest_cache`", but it means the "byte-identical without cache_dir" property is only reachable via direct `build_command` calls — no runner path exercises it, so a future regression there is unguarded by execution (only by the argv unit test, which does cover it). The INFRA "identical shape" retry also now differs from the parallel attempt's argv in the cache-dir path segment.
findings.suggestion: Either pass `cache_dir` only where the narrow path needs it, or add one assertion (unit or integration) that a whole-unit/INFRA retry's argv shape matches the first attempt's apart from the tmp path.

findings.finding: Collection errors can enter the failed-only path. Under xdist, a failed module can produce one `lastfailed` entry and one JUnit error testcase, satisfying this cross-check. Because collection aborted the initial run, other modules may never have executed; retrying only the failed module can nevertheless mark the unit green. AC-7 explicitly requires whole-unit fallback for collection errors, but the integration test permits `"failed-only"`.
findings.suggestion: Detect collection failures and force the whole-unit serial retry. Test with a separate healthy module and verify that its tests execute before the unit becomes green.

findings.finding: The merge drops every original failure without verifying that the retry actually reran each failed testcase. For example, if two tests originally fail and dynamic collection removes one before retry, the remaining test can pass with rc 0; this merge deletes both failures and returns a smaller green report. It also accepts arbitrary well-formed XML containing no testcases. This violates AC-4’s complete-report guarantee and bypasses AC-2’s fallback.
findings.suggestion: Validate the retry testcase keys and resulting total before writing a successful merge. Missing replacements, ambiguous duplicates, or unexpected count changes should return `False` and trigger the whole-unit retry.

findings.finding: The coverage assertion checks only whether filenames appear in coverage’s `file` table, which does not prove coverage was appended. `only_ok` is imported at module scope during retry, and source discovery can include files with no executed lines. Consequently, erased first-attempt coverage could still satisfy these assertions.
findings.suggestion: Read recorded executed lines through `CoverageData` and assert that the body of `only_ok.value()`, executed exclusively by the initial green test, remains covered after retry. Verify that replacing append with overwrite makes this test fail.  Ship-with-fixes: the approach is sound, but collection-error handling and merge validation can currently certify incomplete runs as green. The coverage probe also needs to verify retained executed lines.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
